<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the top-level of the PKGBUILD and does not execute functions such as `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`. In this PKGBUILD, the global scope contains only standard variable assignments (e.g., `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, `sha256sums`) and function definitions. There are no top-level command substitutions, immediate executions, or side-effecting expressions that would trigger during sourcing.

Notably, the `source` array references a git repository from the project's own upstream (`https://github.com/indexable-inc/blaze`), and the `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is normal for VCS-based packages and does not pose a risk during `--printsrcinfo`. The `_srcenv` function and others are defined but not called at parse time. No network operations, file modifications, or data exfiltration occur during sourcing.

Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe, as it will not execute any malicious or unintended code.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No top-level execution of malicious code</summary>
</security_assessment>

The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is appropriate for VCS sources and does not indicate a security issue. The build process uses `cargo fetch --locked`, `cargo build --release --frozen`, and `cargo test`, all of which are standard and safe practices for Rust packages, ensuring reproducibility and dependency integrity.

The `_srcenv` function sets common Cargo environment variables and respects debug/LTO options via `check_option`, which is a typical pattern in AUR PKGBUILDs. No network requests, file downloads, or system modifications occur outside the build environment. Installation is limited to placing compiled binaries in `/usr/bin` and license files in the proper directory. There are no obfuscated commands, unexpected file operations, or data exfiltration attempts.

All dependencies are legitimate Rust build tools or system libraries. The package provides and conflicts with the base name as expected. No dangerous commands (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`, `base64` decoding) are present. The code is transparent, maintainable, and consistent with AUR packaging norms.
</details>

The use of "manual" as a source type does not indicate malicious intent or even unusual behavior—it is a legitimate and commonly used option in nvchecker configurations.

No obfuscation, suspicious URLs, or data exfiltration mechanisms are present. The file does not interact with the system or external resources by itself and poses no security risk.
